survey: Retro fuel pump standing on a square concrete slab in a desert, seen at a slight three-quarter angle. Parts: (1) a rounded orange cabinet with its front facing the camera; (2) a flat cap on top, with a red top and a white rim, held on a short dark stem that comes out of the top of the cabinet; (3) a recessed window on the front with a 5-digit mechanical counter (73608) and two small buttons/slots under it; (4) a round analog dial below it with a red needle, set flush in the front panel; (5) a framed holster recess on the right side, where the orange nozzle hangs with its spout hooked into the top of the boot; (6) a black hose that leaves the nozzle's grey ferrule, drops toward the slab, loops and goes back into the lower side of the cabinet; (7) grey plinth blocks at the foot of the cabinet, styled as weathered or chipped, that sit firmly on the slab. Every part attaches somewhere real. The cap rests on its stem, the nozzle sits in its holster, the hose is connected at both ends (nozzle and cabinet), and the pump stands flat on the slab with nothing floating. Parts are simplified (one dial, one counter, no price display) but this is acceptable simplification, not a construction fault.
